newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates rise in week--FHLMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates rise in week--FHLMC.

text.p: The average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages rose in the week ending January 3, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Thursday.
The 30-year interest rate averaged 7.67 percent in the week, up from 7.64 percent the previous week, while the 15-year inched up to 7.18 percent from 7.16 percent last week.
But adjustable-rate mortgages dipped to an average 5.56 percent from 5.57 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.02 percent, the 15-year 6.56 percent, and the ARM 5.46 percent.
"Rates rose a little earlier in the week and that may well be reflected in slightly higher interest rates in the coming week," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
But he added, "still, we expect interest rates to remain in the 7.5 percent to eight percent range at least for the foreseeable future."
On Tuesday the Commerce Department reported a 14.2 percent jump in U.S. November new home sales to a 772,000 unit annual rate.
And on Monday the National Association of Realtors said that U.S. sales of existing homes rose 1.8 percent in November.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans in the week, both unchanged from last week. They charged 1.4 percent on the ARM, up from 1.3 percent the previous week.
